block.loconautics.analog_controller.tool: Drives a train, sending _throttle_ and _steering_ over Redstone Link frequencies.
Sneak Click on Axle or Transmission
_Copies_ that block's frequencies onto this item.
block.loconautics.bearing_axle.tooltip.s: The _driving wheel_ of a carriage, steered by _Left_ and _Right_ signals.
block.loconautics.bearing_axle.tooltip.c: Sneak Click on an Analog Controller
block.loconautics.bearing_axle.tooltip.b: _Copies_ the controller's Left and Right frequencies onto this item.
block.loconautics.handbrake.tooltip.summ: A _parking brake_ for a single carriage, it locks the car to the rail.
block.loconautics.handbrake.tooltip.beha: _Holds_ the carriage in place so it can't be driven or roll down a slope.
block.loconautics.brake_controller.toolt: An _inline brake_ for the drive shaft. It passes rotation through and _slows_ the output, the _higher_ the lever position, the _harder_ it brakes.
Placed between an Engine and a Transmission
Only works _on the shaft line_ with an engine on one end and a Transmission on the other. Anywhere else it does nothing.
The output turns _slower_ with every step, down to a _quarter_ of its speed at full brake. The wheels brake with it.
While the Emergency Frequency has a Signal
Brakes at _full force_: the shaft _stops_ and the wheels _lock_, whatever the lever says.
block.loconautics.speedometer.tooltip.su: Measures the _speed_ and _distance_ of the carriage it sits on. Panel gauges can show speed, odometer, trip and a clock.
block.loconautics.speedometer.tooltip.be: Outputs a signal from 0 to 15, full at _180 km/h_.
block.loconautics.speed_sign.tooltip.sum: A _speed limit_ sign on a post, two blocks tall. It only _informs_ the driver and does not slow the train.
block.loconautics.speed_sign.tooltip.beh: Click the _sign_ for the next limit, click the _post_ for the previous one.
block.loconautics.clearance_sign.tooltip: A _line sign_ on a post, two blocks tall. Warns of a place with _restricted clearance_ ahead, such as a tunnel or a bridge. Informative only.
block.loconautics.whistle_sign.tooltip.s: A _line sign_ with a big letter C. The driver must _sound the whistle_ at this point. Informative only.
A red and white _line sign_. The track _ends_ here, buffer stop ahead. Informative only.
A _line sign_ showing a rise in the track. The line climbs or drops from this point. Informative only.
block.loconautics.station_border_sign.to: A blue _line sign_ that marks the _boundary of a station_. Informative only.
Tanks can be 5 blocks wide at most
Stores _Fluids_. Lays down along the face you click, so it can stand or lie.
Holds _12,000mb_ per block. Every touching tank joins into one, in any shape up to _5_ blocks wide.
When Placed on a Tank End
Places a whole layer at once. _Sneak_ to place a single block.
When Right Clicked with a Wrench
Switches the _windows_ of the whole tank on or off.
block.loconautics.industrial_pump.toolti: Moves _Fluids_ through a pipe network, reaching _further_ than a regular Mechanical Pump.
Pushes fluid _further_ down the pipes, following whatever Create's own pump range is set to.
block.loconautics.knuckle.tooltip.summar: An _automatic coupler_ that locks two train carriages together.
block.loconautics.knuckle.tooltip.behavi: _Locks_ together on a pivot, so the cars hold as one train and still take corners.
_Uncouples_ a connected knuckle, or _rotates_ one that is not coupled.
block.loconautics.locomotive_gauge.toolt: A panel that reads _one value_ off a boiler. _Four_ fit on a block face.
When Used on a Source Block
_Binds_ the gauge to it. A gauge that is not bound cannot be placed.
block.loconautics.dashboard.tooltip.summ: A sloped _control desk_. Holds _two_ panel parts per block and joins its neighbors into one run.
block.loconautics.dashboard.tooltip.cond: When Right Clicked with a Panel Part
block.loconautics.dashboard.tooltip.beha: Fits the part into the _left_ or _right_ half you aimed at.
Joins into one run, up to _5_ blocks long.
block.loconautics.dashboard.tooltip.cond: Sneak Click a Part with a Wrench
block.loconautics.smart_safety_valve.too: Vents the boiler on its own once _steam pressure_ passes a set point.
Leaves _no headroom_, and the boiler can still burst.
block.loconautics.smokestack.tooltip.sum: Lets a boiler _vent_ its waste gas and tints the smoke.
block.loconautics.transmission.tooltip.s: A gearbox that turns a _Speed_ signal into rotation, with a _Direction_ signal to flip it.
block.loconautics.transmission.tooltip.c: Sneak Click on an Analog Controller
block.loconautics.transmission.tooltip.b: _Copies_ the controller's Speed and Direction frequencies onto this item.
block.loconautics.turntable_bearing.tool: A bearing that turns a plate to _exact angles_ and holds them.
Sneak Click with a Train Signal
_Binds_ the signal. It stays red while the plate is away from home or holds a train.

item.loconautics.hose.tooltip.summary: Carries _fluid_ from a winch to a nozzle.
item.loconautics.hose.tooltip.condition1: Right Click a Winch, then a Nozzle
item.loconautics.hose.tooltip.behaviour1: Runs a hose between the two, in _either_ order.
item.loconautics.locomotive_valve.toolti: A hand wheel for a _Locomotive Gauge_ panel. Bind it to a _Safety Valve_ before placing.

item.loconautics.steel_cable.tooltip.sum: A heavy _cable_ for joining rope holders over _long distances_.

item.loconautics.steel_cable.tooltip.beh: Creates a strand with _twice_ the range of a standard rope.

loconautics.configuration.experimental.b: Firebox, boiler body, smokestack and the rest of the steam blocks. Not finished yet. Off hides them, stops them being placed and removes their recipes. Needs a restart.
loconautics.configuration.experimental.d: The small combustion engines. Not finished yet. Off hides them, stops them being placed and removes their recipes. Needs a restart.
loconautics.configuration.experimental.i: Industrial pipes, pump, valve, tank and cerisene. Not finished yet. Off hides them, stops them being placed or used and removes their recipes. Needs a restart.
loconautics.configuration.experimental.s: The screw link coupler. Not finished yet. Off hides it, stops it being placed and removes its recipe. Needs a restart.
loconautics.configuration.experimental.h: The handbrake. Not finished yet. Off hides it, stops it being placed and removes its recipe. Needs a restart.
loconautics.configuration.train.maxBogey: Maximum Create bogeys allowed in one carriage (glued cluster). Default 2, matching Create.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.bearing: Stress multiplier for a Bearing Axle driving against the rest of its train.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.turntab: Stress Units used by a Turntable Bearing per RPM of plate speed.
loconautics.configuration.boiler.burnRat: Multiplies how fast a lit boiler burns fuel. Water use and pressure are not changed.
loconautics.configuration.boiler.maxLeng: Most body blocks a boiler may span along its length before it stops working. Longer boilers burn more fuel and draw more water.
loconautics.configuration.boiler.maxLeve: Highest level a boiler can reach. The level is the lowest of its size and its fire.
loconautics.configuration.boiler.fireLev: Levels each firebox adds to the fire limit with normal fuel.
Levels each firebox adds to the fire limit with poor fuel like wood.
Levels each firebox adds to the fire limit with premium fuel like coal blocks.
loconautics.configuration.boiler.poorFue: Fuel that burns this many ticks or less counts as poor, unless a fuel tag says otherwise.
loconautics.configuration.boiler.premium: Fuel that burns longer than this many ticks counts as premium, unless a fuel tag says otherwise.
loconautics.configuration.boiler.suPerLe: Stress units a boiler gives for each level at full pressure.
loconautics.configuration.boiler.bankedB: Share of full burn a lit boiler keeps when its master signal is 15.
loconautics.configuration.boiler.warmupP: Extra warmup ticks for each size level above 3.
loconautics.configuration.compat.compute: Allows computers to control trains, signals, points and turntables by ID. Turning this off limits control to computers inside the train.
loconautics.configuration.foundation.ena: Allows stations to assemble standard Create trains.
Allows stations to assemble Loconautics physics trains.
loconautics.configuration.track.derailme: A carriage reaching a track end slower than this, in blocks per second, stops there instead of running off.
How much a collision must change a carriage's speed, in blocks per second, to derail it.
Allows coupled carriages in the same train to derail each other when they collide.
Off, a car leans outward on its springs in a curve and its wheels stay on the rail. On, the wheels lift from the real overturning force and a car taken too fast tips off.
Allows a strong upward push, such as from a Physics Staff, to lift a train off the rails.
How many times its own weight an upward pull must lift a carriage with before it leaves the rail.
Maximum angle in degrees that a rail can tilt away from level before a train derails.
The lift limit while the Physics Staff drags a carriage. At 0 the Physics Staff never lifts a carriage off the rail.
loconautics.configuration.train.dynamics: Acceleration for a train at the reference mass.
How quickly the brakes slow a train, regardless of its mass.
A train of this mass uses the base acceleration. Lighter trains accelerate faster and heavier ones more slowly.
Controls how quickly a coasting train slows down. Set to 0 to disable rolling resistance.
Adds stress to working Bearing Axles when the train climbs a slope.
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_row_powe: Power and Fuel of Engine Rows

Speed is set by the slowest running engine

block.loconautics.small_combustion_engin: A _six cylinder_ engine that turns a shaft by burning _liquid fuel_ from a bucket or pipe.
_Slows down_ as the signal gets stronger, and _stops_ at full strength.
Keeps chunks loaded around physics trains stopped at stations.
loconautics.configuration.train.relocati: Allows players to move physics trains with a Wrench.
Limits Wrench relocation to trains that have derailed.
loconautics.configuration.track.railSear: Horizontal search radius in blocks when looking for nearby track.
loconautics.configuration.track.derailme: Allows trains to derail when they hit the end of the track.
Scales the drive force of a derailed train on the ground. Set to 0 to disable this movement.
loconautics.configuration.track.rerail.a: Allows trains and off-track bogeys to return to nearby rails automatically.
Maximum speed at which a train can begin rerailing automatically.
loconautics.configuration.hatch.injector: Water storage capacity of fluid hatches and supported Hullsteel sockets, in millibuckets.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.analog_: Ticks between steps toward zero throttle when the controller is unattended, unlocked and free of schedule control.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.transmi: Stress Units used by a Transmission per RPM of output speed.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.brake_c: Stress Units the Brake Controller adds per RPM at full braking. A released brake adds none.
loconautics.configuration.items.steel_ca: Maximum distance in blocks between two ends of a Steel Cable.
loconautics.configuration.couplers.knuck: Ticks between scans for new knuckle coupler connections.
loconautics.configuration.hose.maxLength: Maximum length in blocks for a hose connection.
loconautics.configuration.explosions.sub: Allows explosions to push nearby Sable contraptions.
Scales the knockback radius based on the explosion's power.
Scales how strongly an explosion pushes nearby contraptions.
Adds an upward component to the explosion's knockback.
loconautics.configuration.patch.enableRo: Allows Mechanical Rollers to work on moving Sable contraptions.
loconautics.configuration.patch.enablePl: Allows Mechanical Ploughs to work on moving Sable contraptions.
loconautics.configuration.patch.requireM: Controls whether the Create patches should consume materials for block placement.
loconautics.configuration.gauges.dialWob: Needle wobble in degrees on gauges. Set to 0 to keep the needle steady.
loconautics.ponder.dashboard_desk.text_1: Dashboards are sloped desks that hold panel parts
loconautics.ponder.dashboard_desk.text_2: Each Dashboard holds 2 parts, one on each side
loconautics.ponder.dashboard_desk.text_3: Dashboards placed side by side join into one desk of up to 5
loconautics.ponder.dashboard_desk.text_4: Using a Wrench configures the part it points at
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_1: The Firebox burns fuel to heat a Boiler
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_2: Right click it with any furnace fuel to light it
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_3: It holds a single stack and burns it faster under load
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_4: An empty hand will swing the doors open or closed
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_5: Using a Shovel scrapes the fire back out
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_6: A Firebox Stoker underneath holds 9 stacks of fuel
loconautics.ponder.boiler_assembly.text_: Boiler Body blocks touching the Firebox form the barrel
A Smokestack on top of any body block lets waste gas out
Water enters through a Fluid Hatch touching a body block
A Steam Takeoff against the barrel turns steam into rotation
Engineer's Goggles on the Firebox name the next missing piece
loconautics.ponder.boiler_ratio.text_1: One Firebox can heat 3 Boiler Body blocks
loconautics.ponder.boiler_ratio.text_2: Too much barrel leaves the boiler underfired and below full pressure
loconautics.ponder.boiler_ratio.text_3: Too much fire gains nothing and burns fuel faster
loconautics.ponder.boiler_ratio.text_4: The Efficiency reading shows how well the two match
loconautics.ponder.boiler_smokestack.tex: Waste gas leaves through a Smokestack on any body block
Without a stack, gas builds up in the barrel...
...and chokes the output completely after 45 seconds
Fitting the stack clears the gas twice as fast
The smoke color shows how hot the boiler is running
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_1: A Fluid Hatch against a body block is a water inlet
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_2: Hose Nozzles can dock into it to fill the boiler
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_3: Using a Fluid Pipe on the barrel places a Barrel Pipe Connector
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_4: Pipes alone will not move any water
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_5: A powered Mechanical Pump will push the water in
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_6: The connector only takes water in, it cannot drain the boiler
loconautics.ponder.boiler_takeoff.text_1: Steam Takeoffs against the barrel generate Rotational Force
loconautics.ponder.boiler_takeoff.text_2: Speed follows the pressure, from 4 to 128 RPM
loconautics.ponder.boiler_takeoff.text_3: Stress Capacity depends on the size of the barrel
loconautics.ponder.boiler_takeoff.text_4: Without the boiler, the shaft winds down in 3 seconds
loconautics.ponder.boiler_pressure.text_: A burning, watered boiler builds up pressure
Working pressure is 1.0, and it bursts at 1.6
Safety Valves vent the pressure from the barrel
Right click a Safety Valve with a Valve to bind it
Smart Safety Valves vent by themselves at 3/4 of burst pressure
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_1: A hot boiler with no water will fail in 30 seconds...
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_2: ...but refilling it brings the countdown down twice as fast
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_3: A full fire against a shut valve will burst the barrel
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_4: Waste gas only chokes the output, it never explodes
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_5: The blast scales with the size of the barrel
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_6: In Arcade mode it locks out, and a Shovel resets it
loconautics.ponder.boiler_gauge.text_1: Right click a Firebox with a Locomotive Gauge to bind it
loconautics.ponder.boiler_gauge.text_2: It can be placed on any face in the same level
loconautics.ponder.boiler_gauge.text_3: Using a Wrench on it opens its settings
loconautics.ponder.boiler_gauge.text_4: Gauges also read speedometers, stressometers and fluid valves
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_1: Panels hold up to 4 parts, one in each quadrant
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_2: A lone part sits centered until a second one moves it to a corner
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_3: Aim at a free quadrant to place the next part there
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_4: Sneak and right click with a Wrench to take a part back
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_5: Breaking the panel takes its parts out one at a time
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_1: Controls are bound to a Redstone Link receiver first
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_2: A Gauge Button sends a full signal for 1 second
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_3: A Gauge Switch holds the signal until it is toggled
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_4: A Gauge Lever is analog, drag it from 0 to 15
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_5: Two controls on one link do not fight, the strongest wins
loconautics.ponder.panel_gui.text_1: Using a Wrench on a part opens its Interface
loconautics.ponder.panel_gui.text_2: The top bar holds a label for the part
loconautics.ponder.panel_gui.text_3: The Signal row takes 2 Items that set the Frequency it sends on
loconautics.ponder.panel_gui.text_4: The preview shows the part as it will look
loconautics.ponder.panel_gui.text_5: The arrows and dots below it switch between styles
loconautics.ponder.panel_look.text_1: The Body column picks the casing of the part
loconautics.ponder.panel_look.text_2: The Color column paints the cap, knob or wheel
loconautics.ponder.panel_look.text_3: Toggles add a Plate, a Light or a Glass case
loconautics.ponder.panel_look.text_4: Invert swaps the signal, on sends off and off sends on
loconautics.ponder.panel_look.text_5: Confirm applies the new look to the part
loconautics.ponder.panel_glass.text_1: A closed Glass case keeps a part from being used
loconautics.ponder.panel_glass.text_2: Sneak and right click to open the case
loconautics.ponder.panel_glass.text_3: Once the case is open the part works as usual
loconautics.ponder.panel_glass.text_4: Sneak and right click again to close it
loconautics.ponder.panel_targets.text_1: Panel parts can be bound to any block that accepts Redstone
loconautics.ponder.panel_targets.text_2: The part powers the block directly, no Link is needed
loconautics.ponder.panel_targets.text_3: The part stays bound when another block takes its place
loconautics.ponder.panel_targets.text_4: Rails, Doors and Machines answer to it the same way
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_single.h: Generating Rotational Force using Small Combustion Engines
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_single.t: Small Combustion Engines burn liquid fuel to generate Rotational Force
Right click it with a bucket of fuel to fill its tank
Rotational Force will be output through the shaft on its front
At most it provides 256 RPM and 8192 Stress Units
Cerisene is the best fuel, while Lava is the weakest
Engineer's Goggles will show whether it is running or out of fuel
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_pipes.te: Fuel is received through the bottom of the engine
A Fluid Tank and Pipes can supply it
Pipes alone will not move any fuel
Once powered, the pump will push fuel into the engine...
...which will run until the tank is empty
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_tandem.t: Engines placed in a line facing the same way will connect...
...and switch to models that fit together
A row can hold up to 3 Engines
The front Engine outputs the Rotational Force of the whole row
Each running engine adds 8192 Stress Units to the output
Fuel is shared, and a broken engine passes its own on
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_redstone: Without a Redstone signal engines run at full speed
Every point of signal strength slows them by a sixteenth
A signal of 8 leaves half of the speed
At 14 the engines run at their slowest
A signal of 15 will turn them off
A signal at any engine of the row controls the whole row
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_panel.te: Right click an Engine with a Gauge Lever to bind it
Its power acts as a Redstone signal, 15 turns the engine off
A Gauge Switch works the other way round, on is full speed
A Valve is bound the same way
It goes from full speed to the slowest, never off
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_1: Hose Winches attach flat to any block face
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_2: Rotational Force will reel the hose in or out
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_3: The direction of rotation decides if the hose is paid out or hauled in
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_4: A faster rotation reels the hose faster
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_5: Breaking the winch snaps the hose and drops the Hose item
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch_free.text_: An unpowered Hose Winch only reels while Rotational Force drives it
A Redstone signal lets the winch spin free and pay out hose as it is pulled
While paying out, the winch turns its shaft and generates Rotational Force
Reeling the hose back in still takes Rotational Force
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_1: A Hose joins a Hose Winch to a Hose Nozzle or a Hose Connector
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_2: Right click the winch with a Hose, then the nozzle
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_3: A line previews the run while one end is selected
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_4: Sneak and Right click to drop the selection
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_5: A hose can only be paid out up to its maximum length
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_1: Right click a nozzle with empty hands to hold it
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_2: Scrolling pushes it out or pulls it closer
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_3: Holding the rotate key while moving the mouse turns it
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_4: Near an open Nozzle Socket, a nozzle docks itself upright
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_5: A taut hose pulls a docked nozzle out of its socket
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_1: Hoses need a Mechanical Pump on the face opposite the mount
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_2: Pump speed sets how far the pressure reaches...
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_3: ...a hose only works once the pressure covers its whole length
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_4: Docked in a Nozzle Socket, everything pumped goes into it
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_5: A reversed pump pulls Fluid back out through the hose
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_6: A loose nozzle sprays what is pumped, and the jet pushes it back
loconautics.ponder.hose_connector.text_1: Hose Connectors attach to the face of any block that holds Fluids
loconautics.ponder.hose_connector.text_2: Right click a Hose Winch with a Hose, then the connector
loconautics.ponder.hose_connector.text_3: Fluid pumped through the hose enters the block behind the plate...
loconautics.ponder.hose_connector.text_4: ...and a reversed pump pulls it back out the same way
loconautics.ponder.hose_connector.text_5: Using a Wrench on it removes the newest hose, then the connector itself
loconautics.ponder.hose_rope_connector.t: Rope Connectors can hold a Hose as well as a Rope
A winch can reel its Hose in to a Rope Connector...
...and a second Hose carries on to a Hose Connector
Fluid follows the chain of hoses to the last connector or nozzle
Each Rope Connector holds at most 2 Hoses, one in and one out
A single Hose stretches up to 28 Blocks by default
A chain can pass through up to 16 Hoses
Fluid reaches the last Tank no matter how many Rope Connectors it crosses
Hose Connectors only move Fluids as far as the pump can push
At low speed the Fluid stops short of the connector
At high speed it reaches the end of the Hose
A reversed pump needs that same speed to pull Fluids back
loconautics.ponder.hose_connector_link.t: A Hose can join two Hose Connectors directly, no Winch needed
Right click one connector with a Hose, then the other
A Pump behind one connector pushes Fluids through the Hose...
...into whatever holds Fluids behind the other connector
Each Hose Connector holds a single Hose and cannot relay to another
loconautics.ponder.nozzle_socket.text_1: Nozzle Sockets hold a nozzle upright and take its Fluid
loconautics.ponder.nozzle_socket.text_2: Right click the lid to open it
loconautics.ponder.nozzle_socket.text_3: A nozzle that comes near an open socket docks itself
loconautics.ponder.nozzle_socket.text_4: Alone, a socket stores Water in its own tank
loconautics.ponder.nozzle_socket.text_5: With a Fluid Tank behind it, the Fluid goes there instead
loconautics.ponder.nozzle_socket.text_6: A Redstone signal shuts docking and pops the nozzle out
A Nozzle Socket touching a Boiler Body is a water inlet
A docked nozzle pours its Water through the socket into the boiler
Without a nozzle the socket keeps Water in its own tank...
...and the Firebox draws from it until the boiler is full
A Boiler Body only takes in Water
loconautics.ponder.transmission_single.t: Transmissions relay Rotational Force and set its speed from a signal
Rotational Force enters through the shaft on one end
With no signal the output stays still
A Redstone signal on one side sets the output speed
The output grows with the strength of the signal
At full strength it turns at 256 RPM
loconautics.ponder.transmission_directio: A signal on the opposite side reverses the output
The speed stays the same while the direction flips
loconautics.ponder.transmission_frequenc: Right click it with empty hands to open its Interface
The Speed row is the frequency that sets the output speed
The Direction row is the frequency that reverses it
Redstone Links on the same frequencies now control the Transmission
loconautics.ponder.transmission_panel.te: Sneak and Right click a Transmission with a Gauge Lever to bind it
Dragging the lever sets the speed of the Transmission
A Gauge Switch bound the same way sets the direction
Redstone signals are ignored while a panel drives it
loconautics.ponder.brake_controller_sing: The Brake Controller passes rotation straight through, from one end to the other
It only fits between an engine and a Transmission, all on the same shaft line
With the brake released the shaft keeps its full speed
Pulling the brake slows the output side, the harder the slower
At full brake the output slows to a quarter of its speed
loconautics.ponder.brake_controller_freq: Right click it with empty hands to open its Interface
The Brake row is the frequency that sets the brake, the lever position is the strength
The Emergency row is a second frequency, while it has a signal the brake bites at full force
Sneak and right click an Analog Controller with the item in hand to copy its frequency
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_wheels.tex: Bearing Axles drive the wheels of the bogey they sit beside
They have to touch the bogey on its rail line, never above or below
A bogey can only be driven by one Bearing Axle
Engineer's Goggles show whether an axle is valid
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_front.head: Setting the Front of a Locomotive
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_front.text: Bearing Axles mark the front of a locomotive
The front is the side of the axle that touches the bogey
The shaft end of the axle is always the rear
Assembly and Stations use that end to tell which way the train faces
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_drive.head: Powering Locomotives with Transmissions
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_drive.text: A Transmission goes on the shaft end of the Bearing Axle
A Portable Engine provides the Rotational Force on the other side
Burning fuel in the engine starts the rotation
The Portable Engine is only a demonstration, any Rotational Force works
A Creative Motor can power the Transmission as well
And so can a spinning Water Wheel
A Speed signal decides how fast the Bearing Axle turns
Binding Bearing Axles to Redstone Links
Right click it with empty hands to open its Interface
The Left row is the frequency that steers the train left
The Right row is the frequency that steers it right
Each frequency is made of two Items, like a Redstone Link
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_controls.t: Analog Controllers send the signals that drive a locomotive
Sneak and Right click it to open its Interface
Speed and Direction are the frequencies the Transmission listens to
Left and Right are the frequencies the Bearing Axle listens to
Right click a Controller while Sneaking to copy them onto a block
Sneak and Right click in the air to clear the copied frequencies
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_assembly.t: A locomotive needs a Bearing Axle and a Transmission on its bogey
Right click the Station to open its Interface
The New Train button switches the Station to Assembly mode
Assemble as Sable Train builds the locomotive as a physics train
Raising the Analog Controller output steps the train up to speed
Letting go steps the output and the train back down
Hold Space near a Station to park the train on it
A Physics Assembler can also turn a train back into blocks
loconautics.ponder.analog_controller_int: Analog Controllers send throttle and steering over Redstone Link frequencies
Right click one to take control of it
Holding forward raises the output one level at a time
Letting go steps the output back down
Sprint locks the output where it is
The mouse wheel sets the highest level the output can reach
loconautics.ponder.analog_controller_fre: Binding Analog Controllers to Redstone Links
Sneak and Right click it to open its Interface
The Speed row is the frequency sent while driving forward
The Direction row is the one sent while driving backward
The Left row is the frequency sent while steering left
The Right row is the frequency sent while steering right
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_ass: Turntable Bearings attach to the block in front of them
Use Super Glue to select the blocks that will turn with it
Right click the bearing to assemble them
A cogwheel beside the bearing sets how fast it turns
Each Redstone pulse turns it by a set angle
It holds that angle until the next pulse
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_ins: Sneak and Right click it to open its Interface
Turn rotates the structure by an exact angle, up to a full circle
The arrows next to an angle set the direction and double the speed
Delay holds it still for a set time
Await pauses the list until the next Redstone signal
The list stops at End and starts over on the next signal
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_tri: This behavior can be configured using the value panel
Pulse runs the list once for each signal
Repeat While Powered starts the list again until the signal ends
Alternate Direction flips the turn with every signal
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_sch: Setting the first instruction to Schedule lets Train Schedules turn the structure
Rails on it meet the rails of the legs around it
A Train carrying a Schedule for the other leg parks centered on it
It turns the Train to face that leg, no Redstone needed
Then the Train drives off and it turns back to where it started
The cogwheel needs Rotational Force and the structure has to be as long as the Train
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_dia: Reaching Diagonal Legs with Turntable Bearings
A Turntable can turn to any angle, so a leg can leave it diagonally
A Train whose Schedule needs the diagonal leg parks centered on the plate
The plate turns it by whatever angle that leg needs
Then the Train drives straight onto the diagonal leg
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_sig: Binding Train Signals to Turntable Bearings
Sneak and Right click a Turntable Bearing with a Train Signal to bind it
Signals placed afterwards are linked to that bearing
Linked signals stay red while the plate is turning or holds a Train
They turn green again once the plate has settled
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_par: Stations on different legs can share one name, with a * to match them all
A Train sent to that name takes a station that is free
The Turntable turns it toward the leg that has a free station
The Train parks there and the plate returns to its first angle
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_man: Leaving a Parking with Turntable Bearings
A Train parked on a dead end leg has to back out when its Schedule moves on
The plate turns to meet the leg the Train waits on
A Maneuver instruction goes into the Schedule between two destinations
Its speed is a share of full speed, up to 75 percent
The destination after it is where the Train maneuvers to, so it needs one
The Train reverses out of the parking at that speed
It stops centered on the plate
The plate takes the Train and turns it to face the leg it needs next
Then it drives off forward toward its next stop
loconautics.ponder.train_casing_bogeys.t: Holding C with a Train Casing opens the selection menu
Scrolling swaps the Casing for a Bogey
Right click a Track to place the Bogey on it
Train Casings placed between the Bogeys form the body of the train
Glue the blocks together and hold right click on a Physics Assembler
The assembled body counts as a Train and can dock at Stations
loconautics.ponder.train_casing_shaft.te: Bogeys can be fitted with a Shaft by right clicking them with one
Rotation from one side passes straight through, like an encased Shaft
Sneak and Right click with a Wrench to remove the Shaft again
Without the Shaft, rotation stops at the Bogey
block.loconautics.track_switch.tooltip.s: Sets a nearby _track junction_. In auto mode scheduled trains set it along their route, a chosen branch is _locked_ for every train.
block.loconautics.track_switch.tooltip.b: The first empty-hand click binds a junction within _4 blocks_ in _auto_ mode. Further clicks cycle branches clockwise from north, then return to auto. Sneak and right click rebinds and clears the manual choice.
Each pulse picks the _next branch_, after the last one the stand goes back to auto.
loconautics.track_switch.bound: Bound to the nearest junction, auto mode
loconautics.track_switch.lost: The junction is gone, bind again
loconautics.track_switch.free: Auto: scheduled trains set the switch themselves
loconautics.track_switch.status.auto: AUTO · scheduled trains choose their route
loconautics.track_switch.controls: Empty-hand right click: bind / next branch → auto
block.loconautics.retarder_track.tooltip: A _Create track_ that brakes a train down to a set speed while it is powered. It never stops the train, a train that is already slower is left alone.
Cars on this rail are slowed down to the _chosen speed_.
Click the _top_ for the next speed, click a _side_ for the previous one.
When Laid as a Long Piece
The _whole piece_ between two clicks brakes, not only its end blocks. Power at _either end_ is enough.
block.loconautics.safety_unit.tooltip.su: Runs the _safety systems_ of the carriage it sits on. Place it anywhere in the consist, front towards the direction of travel. Needs a Speedometer on the same carriage.
block.loconautics.safety_unit.tooltip.be: Opens the list of safety systems. Each can be switched, and bound to a toggle by a _Redstone Link_ frequency.
Holds the _emergency brake_ until the carriage has stopped. Outputs 15 to a comparator meanwhile.
gui.loconautics.safety.bind.tooltip: Binds the toggle frequency from the items in your hands: main hand first, off hand second. The system then runs only while the frequency has a signal.
gui.loconautics.safety.clear.tooltip: Removes the toggle, the system follows its switch only
gui.loconautics.safety.invert.tooltip: Turn on when the unit sees the train roll back although it drives right. The front of the block is forward.
loconautics.safety.bind_empty: Hold a frequency item in your hand first
block.loconautics.typhon.tooltip.summary: A standalone _locomotive air horn_ controlled by _Redstone Link_ or redstone. Emits a steam jet and horn blast while powered.
block.loconautics.typhon.tooltip.behavio: Binds the _Redstone Link_ frequency from your main hand and off-hand items.
loconautics.typhon.bind_hint: Hold frequency items in your hands to bind
block.loconautics.air_compressor.tooltip: Pumps compressed air into adjacent _Air Reservoirs_ using rotational force.
loconautics.emergency_brake.goggles.head: Emergency Brake:
Stores compressed air up to _8.5 bar_ and equalizes pressure with adjacent reservoirs.
block.loconautics.driver_brake_valve.too: Controls _brake pipe pressure_ across the consist. Can be bound to a _Panel Valve_ or _Locomotive Gauge_.
block.loconautics.triple_valve.tooltip.s: Applies car brakes proportionally when _brake pipe pressure_ drops. _Shift-click_ when uncoupled to bleed air.
block.loconautics.brake_hose_connector.t: Connects _Brake Hoses_ between cars. Click to toggle the angle cock.
item.loconautics.brake_hose.tooltip.summ: Links two _Brake Hose Adapters_ on adjacent cars into a shared brake pipe.
block.loconautics.emergency_brake.toolti: Vents the _brake pipe_ to _0 bar_ when pulled, triggering emergency braking across all coupled cars.
loconautics.gui.goggles.knuckle_broken: Overload failure — use a wrench to repair
item.loconautics.signal_lamp.tooltip.sum: A warning lamp for a _Locomotive Gauge_ panel. Bind it to a train system to show its alarm state.
item.loconautics.signal_lamp.tooltip.con: Compatible blocks — right-click one to bind:
item.loconautics.signal_lamp.tooltip.beh: Driver's Brake Valve — low main reservoir pressure; Small Engine — overheating; Speedometer — powered axle slip; Safety Unit — system alarm; Brake Controller — emergency braking. Shift + right-click in the air to clear the binding.
gui.loconautics.signal_lamp.bind_first: Bind the lamp to a supported train block first
gui.loconautics.status_display.title: Locomotive status
loconautics.ponder.overhead_poles.text_1: Choose a short, standard or tall pole kit to match the required clearance.
loconautics.ponder.overhead_poles.text_2: The kit places the base, mast sections and cantilever head in one operation.
loconautics.ponder.overhead_poles.text_3: Stand on the track side when placing it so the cantilever points over the rails.
loconautics.ponder.overhead_wire.text_1: Connect the contact wire between cantilever heads at a consistent height.
loconautics.ponder.overhead_wire.text_2: The wire has no collision and can be laid as straight horizontal segments.
loconautics.ponder.overhead_pantograph.t: Mount the pantograph on the carriage roof directly below the contact wire.
As the train moves under the wire, the pantograph raises and detects contact.
Contact outputs a redstone signal; without contact, the output is off.
loconautics.ponder.overhead_electric_mot: Place the electric traction motor on the carriage sublevel.
A redstone level from 1 to 15 sets the motor speed up to 256 RPM.
Connect its output shaft to the drivetrain. Pantograph contact can gate the throttle.
block.loconautics.boiler_body.tooltip.su: A boiler casing piece. Combine it with other casing blocks to build a boiler.
block.loconautics.boiler_body.tooltip.be: Forms the boiler shell together with the other casing pieces.
block.loconautics.buffer.tooltip.summary: A carriage buffer that cushions contact between coupled carriages.
block.loconautics.buffer.tooltip.behavio: Cushions contact between the ends of carriages.
Connects a boiler to a pipe network so fluid lines can interface with its casing.
Provides a fluid-line connection point for the boiler.
block.loconautics.copycat_headstock.tool: A carriage headstock with a copycat surface that can mimic a suitable block.
When a block is applied to its surface
Takes the applied material and adopts its appearance.
block.loconautics.firebox.tooltip.summar: The boiler firebox: the chamber where fuel burns and heats the boiler.
block.loconautics.firebox.tooltip.behavi: Burns fuel to heat the boiler.
block.loconautics.firebox_controller.too: A firebox controller for managing fuel feed and boiler operation.
Sends control signals to the firebox.
block.loconautics.firebox_stocker.toolti: A mechanism for feeding fuel into a boiler firebox.
When fuel is available in its input inventory
block.loconautics.fluid_hatch_gray.toolt: A socket for connecting a fluid hose to equipment.
Provides a hose connection point for a fluid system.
block.loconautics.ball.tooltip.summary: A decorative beach ball for dressing up carriages and stations.
block.loconautics.hose_connector.tooltip: A connector node for routing a flexible hose between equipment points.
Allows a hose line to run between compatible connection points.
block.loconautics.hose_nozzle.tooltip.su: A hose nozzle for dispensing fluid from a connected line.
block.loconautics.hose_nozzle.tooltip.co: When fluid is supplied through the hose
block.loconautics.hose_nozzle.tooltip.be: Dispenses fluid through the nozzle outlet.
block.loconautics.hose_winch.tooltip.sum: A mechanical winch for storing and deploying a hose; it is powered by rotation.
block.loconautics.hose_winch.tooltip.beh: Operates the connected hose and controls its deployment.
A transparent industrial Create pipe for transporting fluids while viewing the flow.
When connected to a fluid network
Transports fluid and lets you see it inside the pipe.
block.loconautics.industrial_pipe.toolti: An industrial pipe for transporting fluids through a pipe network.
An industrial smart pipe for controlling fluid flow in a pipe network.
Restricts fluid passage according to its configured filter.
block.loconautics.industrial_valve.toolt: A valve for controlling fluid passage through an industrial pipe network.
Opens or shuts off flow through the pipe.
block.loconautics.screw_link.tooltip.sum: A screw coupling for mechanically linking adjacent carriages.
block.loconautics.screw_link.tooltip.con: When connected to a compatible coupling
block.loconautics.screw_link.tooltip.beh: Creates a flexible mechanical connection between carriages.
A steam takeoff that connects a boiler to a steam pipe network.
When connected to a boiler and pipes
Feeds steam from the boiler into the connected network.
block.loconautics.turntable_plate.toolti: A rotating platform mounted on a turntable bearing.
When placed on a turntable bearing
Forms the platform that the mechanism turns to a selected angle.
A catenary support for mounting and holding the overhead contact wire.
Is assembled from a base, shaft and head.
An overhead contact wire that supplies power to electric train equipment.
Forms an overhead contact line above the track.
block.loconautics.pantograph.tooltip.sum: A pantograph that reaches the contact wire and supplies power to the train.
block.loconautics.pantograph.tooltip.beh: Establishes electrical contact with the overhead line.
block.loconautics.electric_traction_moto: An electric traction motor that converts overhead-line power into rotation on its drive shaft.
Outputs shaft rotation to drive the wheelset.
block.loconautics.clearance_sign.tooltip: When the sign is placed beside a track
Warns of restricted clearance ahead; it does not affect train movement.
block.loconautics.whistle_sign.tooltip.c: When a train passes the sign
block.loconautics.whistle_sign.tooltip.b: Reminds the driver to sound the whistle; it is an informational marker.
When the sign is placed at the end of a track
Marks a dead end and warns of the track stop ahead.
When the sign is placed beside a track
Shows the track gradient; it does not control train speed.
block.loconautics.station_border_sign.to: When the sign is placed at a station boundary
Marks the station boundary for the train driver.
block.loconautics.smokestack.tooltip.beh: Vents waste gas and affects the colour of the emitted smoke.
block.loconautics.air_compressor.tooltip: Compresses air and sends it into adjacent air reservoirs.
Equalizes pressure in the shared air system and stores an air reserve.
block.loconautics.driver_brake_valve.too: When controlled through a bound panel valve or gauge
Changes the brake pipe pressure across the consist.
block.loconautics.triple_valve.tooltip.b: Automatically supplies the car brake cylinder; releases the brake as pressure rises.
block.loconautics.brake_hose_connector.t: Toggles the brake hose angle cock.
block.loconautics.emergency_brake.toolti: Vents the brake pipe and triggers an emergency stop for the consist.
